title: JPMorgan Dangles 11% Yield on Volta’s $5 Billion AI Loan Sale
source_used: Bloomberg text on Yahoo Finance UK ('(Bloomberg) --'). Bloomberg original not opened (HTTP 403).
key_facts: JPMorgan is pitching a yield of about 11% on a $5 billion leveraged-loan sale for Volta Infrastructure Holdings, one of the highest borrowing costs seen in the market for risky debt used to finance the AI boom.
The loan is marketed at 6.25 to 6.5 percentage points above the benchmark rate and 97 to 98 cents on the dollar, which Bloomberg calculates as a yield of roughly 11%.
Earlier loans to neoclouds such as CoreWeave, Lambda and Crusoe came at lower borrowing costs; the Volta deal, which also includes debt for a data center, is a new high in all-in yield.
A $3.7 billion chip loan would buy about 36,000 Nvidia GPUs and a $1.3 billion loan would cash-collateralize a letter of credit for a data-center lease; lenders must buy part of both.

The money finances a data center complex in Norway run by Volta with Bitdeer Technologies Group; Anthropic has signed a six-year agreement for compute capacity at the site, according to people familiar.
The transaction is unrated, which is unusual in the leveraged-loan market and typically stops collateralized loan obligations, the biggest buyers, from buying; commitments are due 14 Oct.
Companies have borrowed roughly $625 billion over two years for AI data centers and other investments; the AI buildout is expected to cost nearly $5 trillion by the end of 2030.
quote_evidence: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is pitching a yield of about 11% on a $5 billion leveraged-loan sale on behalf of Volta Infrastructure Holdings Ltd., one of the highest borrowing costs seen in the market for risky debt that's become popular for financing the AI boom.
Notably the transaction is unrated, one of the people added, asking not to be identified because they're not authorized to speak publicly.
why_it_matters_hint: A new high in borrowing cost for AI chip and data-centre debt shows how much extra return lenders want for riskier AI projects.
